source.title: Safety-Aligned Weights Are Not Enough: Refusal-Teacher-Guided Finetuning Enhances Safety and Downstream Performance under Harmful Finetuning Attacks
source.authors: Seokil Ham; Yubin Choi; Yu-Jin Yang; Seungju Cho; Younghun Kim; Changick Kim

record.file_problem: The main paper text is present and readable. It refers to supplementary material that is not included.
record.tranche_reason: Tests harmful fine-tuning of safety-aligned models with harmful-score outcomes, but uses its own FaaS setup and measure rather than a direct reproduction of the original method and measure.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the standard SFT/two-stage fine-tuning results where harmful-data ratio or user-data size is varied. The p=0 results are clean-data controls, not evidence that benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance relative to an unfine-tuned aligned model. Defense-method comparisons, prompt-classification results, and gradient-conflict or loss-smoothness analyses do not directly measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: A defense paper, but its motivation analysis (Table 1) and SFT baselines (Tables 2–5) report Harmful Score after fine-tuning safety-aligned models on user data with 100–1,250 harmful examples. That is a direct measure of how strongly harmful fine-tuning removes safety (V1). The setting differs from the originals: the authors build their own safety-aligned model by SFT on BeaverTails refusals from base weights, and score with Beaver-Dam-7B HS.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors argue that fine-tuning safety-aligned weights gives a weak initialization, lowering task accuracy while safety still degrades under harmful data. They propose fine-tuning base weights under a safety-aligned Ref-Teacher, using alignment distillation and refusal-feature data filtering, and report lower HS and higher finetuning accuracy across ratios, data sizes, tasks and three models.
record.recipe_differences: Tests harmful user-data fine-tuning of safety-aligned models, including mixed harmful/harmless datasets, but reports Harmful Score rather than a direct refusal rate and uses its own FaaS setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported Harmful Score varies with harmful-prompt ratio, user-data size, and safety-alignment data size.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing harmful user prompts by filtering (SFT*, LLaMAGuard3-8B) keeps HS at about 1.5–4.4 across ratios and data sizes, versus 16–71 without filtering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety erosion under harmful fine-tuning is driven by the harmful examples themselves; filtering them prevents it.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning base weights jointly on user and safety data yields lower HS (0.9–15.7) than fine-tuning safety-aligned weights (2.2–79.8) at the same harmful ratio (Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety imposed jointly during task fine-tuning resists harmful data better than safety pre-trained into the initialization.

record.problems: The relevant outcome is Harmful Score, not refusal rate. Results in the main text are for specific datasets and settings; supplementary experiments referenced by the paper are not present in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcomes in the supplied main text were left out. Defense-method results are method comparisons, while classification and gradient-conflict results do not directly measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Fewer than 100 harmful examples. Production safety-trained chat models: the aligned model is the authors' own SFT-aligned base model. Direct refusal-rate measures.
Entire version. Clean fine-tuning (p=0) is never compared with the aligned model before fine-tuning.
Entire version. Jailbreak prompts appear only as inputs to the prompt classifier.
Entire version. The Ref-Teacher defense does not target token depth and is not measured per position.

missing.what: SFT baseline HS at p=0.1 on other models: Gemma2-9B 26.1±0.3, Qwen2-7B 11.3±0.8. No clean baselines are given for these models.
SFT baseline HS at p=0.1 with other benign tasks: SST2 41.7±7.1, AGNEWS 26.8±1.6, AlpacaEval 23.7. Llama3-8B HS on GSM8K is given as 19.5±2.5 here, inconsistent with 16.2 in Tables 2/3.

record.verdict_notes: This is a defense paper; the V1 evidence comes from baseline/motivation conditions. The 'safety-aligned' model is LoRA/SFT-aligned by the authors from base Llama3-8B, not an official instruct model, which weakens comparability with the originals. Tables 2/3 SFT rows duplicate the Table 1 SA(10,000) runs, so r14–r17 are not independent. HS is the Beaver-Dam-7B harmful fraction on 1,000 BeaverTails test prompts. Supplementary results (pre-aligned LLM, multi-evaluator) are not available.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fewer than 100 harmful examples, refusal rates directly, or a broad range of safety-trained models. Harmful Score is the reported outcome.
No comparison of benignly fine-tuned models with their pre-fine-tuning safety scores.
No per-token KL divergence by response position.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
No test of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Does not test whether data or an objective produces first-token shallowness.
No training that spreads safety across response positions or test of whether such training holds up.
